ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram is a diamond-shaped structure, with a central node in the middle. The central node is connected to the left and to the right respectively to an AC voltage source labeled 1∠0 V; judging from the polarities in the figure, the positive terminals of both voltage sources are on the central-node side, and the negative terminals are respectively on the left-node and right-node sides. The upper-left branch is a 1 Ω resistor, and the upper-right branch is an inductor labeled j1 Ω; the direction of the current arrow beside the inductor is from the top node along the upper-right branch toward the right node. On the vertical center line, between the central node and the top node, there is a 1∠0 A current source, with the arrow upward. In the lower half, another upward 1∠0 A current source, a lower-left branch -j1 Ω, and a lower-right branch 1 Ω can also be seen. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the central node as the reference point and let V_C=0. From the two horizontal 1∠0 V voltage sources and the polarities in the figure, V_C−V_L=1 and V_C−V_R=1 can be obtained, therefore V_L=V_R=−1 V. Let the top node voltage be V_T. Write KCL for the top node, and take the current leaving the top node as positive: the current through the upper-left 1 Ω resistor is (V_T−V_L)/1=V_T+1; the current through the upper-right inductor j Ω, in the direction shown in the figure from the top to the right node, is (V_T−V_R)/j=(V_T+1)/j; the upper current source arrow is upward, indicating that 1 A is injected into the top node, so when “leaving the top node” is taken as positive, its contribution is −1 A. Thus KCL is (V_T+1)+(V_T+1)/j−1=0. Rearranging gives (V_T+1)(1+1/j)=1, namely (V_T+1)(1−j)=1. The required inductor current is I_L=(V_T+1)/j. From the above equation, I_L=1/(1+j) A can be obtained.

raw_record.question_text: What is the current through the inductor in the circuit shown below?

method.method_draft: Set the center node as reference, V_C=0. From the two horizontal 1∠0 V sources and their polarities, read V_C−V_L=1 and V_C−V_R=1, so V_L=V_R=−1 V. Let the top node voltage be V_T. Apply KCL at the top node, taking currents leaving the top node: through the 1 Ω resistor is (V_T−V_L)/1=(V_T+1), through the inductor is (V_T−V_R)/j=(V_T+1)/j, and the upper current source injects 1 A into the top node, so it contributes −1 A leaving. Thus (V_T+1)+(V_T+1)/j−1=0. Solve (V_T+1)(1+1/j)=1, i.e. (V_T+1)(1−j)=1. The inductor current in the shown top-to-right direction is I_L=(V_T+1)/j=1/(1+j) A.
